title: Simultaneous prime-to-ell field sections over separable charts
statement: Let $K$ be a field, let $\ell$ be a prime different from the characteristic of $K$, and let $I$ be a finite set. For each $i\in I$ let $K_i/K$ be a finite separable field extension [def-pc-field-extension, def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], and let $F_i/K_i$ be a finite field extension whose degree is prime to $\ell$. There exists a finite field extension $K'/K$ of degree prime to $\ell$ such that, for every $i$ and every field factor $M$ of the finite etale $K'$-algebra $K_i\otimes_K K'$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], with multiplication $(a\otimes b)(c\otimes d)=ac\otimes bd$, there is a $K_i$-algebra homomorphism $F_i\to M$. A field factor here means a quotient by a maximal ideal, equipped with the maps induced by $K_i\to K_i\otimes_K K'$ and $K'\to K_i\otimes_K K'$. Degrees mean dimensions as vector spaces [def-weil-vector-space-dimension]. The extension $F_i/K_i$ need not be separable, and $I$ may be empty.

source.place: Expose II, proof of Theorem 3.2.1, quasi-Galois extension L/K, Sylow fixed field and the descent argument using Proposition 2.2.6, printed pp. 29--30. This isolates only its simultaneous field-factor assertion, allowing inseparable degrees prime to ell.

from.place: Ancestor proof Step 3 (Verdier duality), through the open-immersion finiteness input to finite exceptional preservation: ILO XIII 3.2.1, the sentence applying IX 1.1 and II 3.2.3 to construct the finite family of commutative diagrams. Expose II, Theorem 3.2.3, printed pp. 30--31, with finite-cover Corollary 2.2.4, printed p. 27; finite form as used in Expose XIII 3.2.1, printed p. 199. On the integral Noetherian sources the finite flat maps have positive constant finite locally free rank; etale sources may be refined by affine opens. Input to the standard-refinement argument: Expose II, Theorem 3.2.1, printed pp. 29--30; finite affine-open refinement using Corollary 2.2.4, printed p. 27. This is the proper-surjection normal form, not the modification/finite-flat normal form of Theorem 3.2.3. Supporting input: Expose II, proof of Theorem 3.2.1, quasi-Galois extension L/K, Sylow fixed field and the descent argument using Proposition 2.2.6, printed pp. 29--30.
